yes.yes: I move crates for the cargo yard.  Thirty yen a pallet if the foreman likes you.

no.yes: Skewers, noodles, whatever fell off a truck.  Everybody has to eat.
Pulling copper out of dead machines.  The scrapyard buys by the kilo.
Parcels.  Anywhere in the district in twenty minutes, no questions about what is inside.
Dishes.  Thousands of dishes.  The cook shouts, I scrub.
Somebody has to clean up after the offices.  Nobody ever sees me, and that is the job.
I keep the department store ledgers straight.  It pays, and it is quiet.
Telecom maintenance.  When the lines go down, I am the reason they come back.
Hospital ward.  Long shifts, short staff, and a lot of people who will not follow the instructions.
Teaching at the district school.  The kids are fine; the budget is not.
Supermarket floor.  I know every shelf.  Do not ask about the sale prices, they change twice a day.
Precinct paperwork.  Forms for the forms.  You would not believe how many people confess to the wrong crime.
Driving.  Routes, fares, and a city that never uses its own crosswalks.
Systems engineering at the corporate office.  Most of it is making somebody else's mistakes survive another quarter.
Executive floor.  Meetings, then meetings about the meetings.
I own a few places.  Hotels, mainly.  Margins are thin, but rooms keep filling.
I move money around.  Mostly other people's.  It is less fun than it sounds.
Hospital surgery.  Implants, grafts, the occasional miracle.  People pay a great deal to avoid a long recovery.
Retired from the district office.  They still ask my opinion, which is the best part.

yes: Rent is a joke and the water is worse.  The Bratva want their cut and the JSDF want to look the other way.
Nobody here has an implant that works.  We buy them used in the back alleys and hope.
The poor end of town: bars on the windows and dogs on the roofs.  Still, it is home.
Food is cheap on the corner, if you do not mind what it was this morning.
Quiet, clean, guarded.  Exactly as it should be.

no: Things are all right.  Work, a flat, a small place at the market.  Do not count on the weather.
Rents go up every year.  The clinics only get busier.  Everybody wants one more upgrade.
We keep our heads down.  The JSDF patrols are polite, the Bratva stay mostly in the east, and I try not to notice either.
It is a decent district.  I would not want to go lower, and I cannot afford to go higher.

dynamic_line: Charging posts?  There is one outside every hospital, and a few outside the shops.  A few hundred yen for a top-up; more for a full charge.  Cheaper than a night in the clinic.
